tip: For location, на (na = on) takes the prepositional case: втором этаже (vtarom etazhe = second floor), not the base form этаж (etazh).
With a fraction like треть (tret = a third), the verb normally stays singular: опоздала (apazdala = was late), not plural.
Numbers from five up take the genitive plural: пятьсот (pyatsot = five hundred) рублей (rubley = of rubles), not рубли (rubli).
Numbers two, three, four take the genitive singular, not plural: четыре кусочка (chetyre kusochka = four pieces), not кусочки (kusochki).
один из (adin iz = one of) is followed by the genitive plural: студентов (studentov = of students).
A reflexive passive uses -ся (sya): соблюдаются (sablyudayutsa = are followed). The doer takes the instrumental: сотрудниками (satrudnikami = by staff).
известно (izvestna = it is known) is an impersonal neuter form with no subject, followed by что (chto = that) and a clause.
в честь (v chest = in honor of) takes the genitive: поэта (paeta = of the poet). It is how Russian says named after someone.
Case, not position, marks roles, so the object can come first: письма (pisma = letters) is the object, почтальон (pachtalyon = postman) the subject.
выглядишь (vyglyadish = you look) takes an adverb, not an adjective: классно (klassna = great) is the -о adverb form.
Russian drops the verb to be in the present; a dash links зарплата (zarplata = salary) and пятьдесят (pyatdesyat = fifty).
In dates the month goes genitive: марта (marta = of March), so восьмое марта (vasmoye marta) reads the eighth of March.
через (cherez) plus a time word means every other one: через день (cherez den) = every other day, not daily.
Floors take на plus the prepositional: на третьем этаже (na tretyem etazhe = on the third floor), never в (v).
который (katory) changes gender to match its noun: площадь (ploshchad) is feminine, so на которой (na katoroy = on which) is feminine.
тише (tishe = quieter) is the comparative of тихо (tikha = quietly), used alone as a command to be quiet.
Moving up a grade uses в plus the accusative: перешла в пятый класс (pereshla v pyaty klass = moved into fifth grade).
Quantity words push the next noun to genitive: полкило сыра (palkilo syra = half a kilo of cheese), not сыр (syr).
самый (samy = most) before an adjective builds the superlative: самый сложный (samy slozhny = the most difficult).
Some masculine nouns take a stressed -у in the prepositional after на (na): счету (schetu), from счёт (schot = account).
After десять (desyat = ten) the noun turns genitive plural: десять градусов (desyat gradusov = ten degrees).
люди (lyudi) has an irregular genitive plural людей (lyudey = of people), used after сотни (sotni = hundreds).
через (cherez) plus the accusative marks a future point: пять лет (pyat let = five years) counts forward from now.
метро (metro) never changes form; к ближайшему (k blizhayshemu = to the nearest) shows dative, but метро stays fixed.
бы makes a request polite and tentative: не могли бы вы (ne magli by vy = could you) is softer than plain можете (mozhete).
спасибо, что (spasiba, chto) plus a past-tense verb means thanks for doing something: написал (napisal = wrote).
хорошо, что (harasho, chto = good that) opens a clause giving the reason you are glad: ты позвонил (ty pazvanil = you called).
накопила денег (nakapila deneg) puts деньги (dengi = money) into genitive to mean saved some money, an unspecified amount, not a named sum.
Paired или... или (ili... ili = either... or) marks the two choices: идём (idyom = we go) or остаёмся (astayomsya = we stay).
After нет (net = there is no) the noun goes genitive: сомнений (samneniy = doubts), never nominative сомнения (samneniya).
